newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SWISS GLENCORE WINS BULGARIA 50,000T WHEAT TENDER.
newsitem.headline: SWISS GLENCORE WINS BULGARIA 50,000T WHEAT TENDER.

text.p: Swiss firm Glencore won a second tender for the import of 50,000 tonnes of wheat in Bulgaria in exchange for exports from the new harvest, an official at Bulgaria's government press centre said on Thursday.
"Glencore was awarded the contract for the import of 50,000 tonnes of grain among 12 companies which bid at the Agriculture ministry tender on May 12 and 13," the official told reporters.
In March Glencore won another tender for the import of the same amount of wheat.
Bulgaria would have to export a total of 131,750 tonnes of wheat from this year's harvest against the 100,000 tonnes imported by Glencore, the official said.
This week's tender was called after Bulgarian trading firm Nada, which won a tender for import of 50,000 tonnes of wheat in March, failed to meet its contractual obligations.
Bulgaria received 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Poland in March to ease its grain shortage, against an agreement to export the same quantity of wheat from the new crop.
Officials said last week Bulgaria needed about 100,000 tonnes of wheat to cover the gap until the new crop.

Experts said the new crop, which is expected to be much better than last year's, will enable Bulgaria to meet its domestic needs, service export commitments under forward contracts and put aside wheat for the State Reserve.
The Agriculture ministry forecasts 1997 wheat output at some 3.0 million tonnes, up from last year's 1.8 million tonnes. Bulgaria's domestic consumption is estimated at some 1.6 million tonnes.

Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 created acute grain shortages earlier this year, which have been overcome in the past three months. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188, 981 4145
